themes_detail.label: Dead and Overgrown Trees Crisis
themes_detail.summary: Crown Heights is experiencing a severe spike in tree-related complaints this week, with 4 dead/dying tree reports (up 967% from 0.4 weekly average) and 8 overgrown tree/branch complaints (up 1500% from 0.5 weekly average), suggesting a possible storm damage or seasonal die-off event requiring urgent Parks Department response.
evidence: 4 dead/dying tree complaints THIS WEEK vs. 0.4 weekly average over 8 weeks (z-score: 5.21)
8 overgrown tree/branch complaints last week vs. 0.5 weekly average over 8 weeks (z-score: 10.61)
8 new tree requests last week vs. 0.4 weekly average (z-score: 15.75) — residents actively requesting replacements
reporting_angles: Did recent storms or weather events trigger tree failures? Interview Parks Department about response timeline.
Are residents in specific blocks (map the complaints) disproportionately affected? Street-level canvassing for safety concerns.

themes_detail.label: Worship Venue Noise Complaints Surge
themes_detail.summary: Noise complaints from houses of worship spiked to 4 reports last week (up 3100% from 0.1 weekly average), a statistically significant anomaly that suggests either a single facility with a new problem or a nascent trend worth investigating before it escalates.
evidence: 4 house of worship noise complaints last week vs. 0.1 weekly average (z-score: 11.72, severity: high)
No prior baseline complaints of this type — represents genuine new pattern, not seasonal recurrence
Residential noise complaints remain elevated at 1315 over 90 days, suggesting noise is a district-wide ambient issue
reporting_angles: File FOIL request to identify which facilities generated complaints; were they from the same venue or multiple locations?
Interview residents in affected blocks about whether this is new amplification, new hours, or new activities at local places of worship.

themes_detail.label: Homeless Assistance Requests Peak
themes_detail.summary: Homeless person assistance complaints surged to 27 reports three weeks ago (up 671% from 3.5 weekly average), indicating a possible encampment spike, service gap, or quality-of-life crisis that may still be unfolding despite the lag in complaint filing.
evidence: 27 homeless person assistance complaints 3 weeks ago vs. 3.5 weekly average over 8 weeks (z-score: 14.17, severity: high)
Community board's repeated budget request for 'Other facilities for homeless' suggests this is a chronic unresolved issue
No follow-up data on whether complaints have normalized or remain elevated — current week status unknown
reporting_angles: Map the 27 complaints geographically — are they clustered in one area (park, transit hub, commercial block) or dispersed?
Contact DHS about whether they deployed resources in response; interview residents and local business owners about visibility and safety.

themes_detail.label: Lead Complaints Double
themes_detail.summary: Lead-related complaints jumped to 10 reports three weeks ago (up 167% from 3.8 weekly average), an anomaly that may reflect either renewed parent/tenant awareness or actual lead hazard incidents in housing stock — requires urgent verification given child health stakes.
evidence: 10 lead complaints 3 weeks ago vs. 3.8 weekly average (z-score: 4.49, severity: high)
Crown Heights has older housing stock and historically higher risk for lead paint hazards
464 DOB building permits filed in last 90 days, including 270 alterations — potential source of disturbed lead paint
reporting_angles: Contact NYC Department of Health to identify which buildings triggered complaints; request any follow-up testing results.
Interview families or tenants about whether complaints stemmed from renovation work, paint deterioration, or new testing/awareness campaigns.

themes_detail.label: Maintenance and Facility Issues Spike
themes_detail.summary: Maintenance or facility complaints surged to 28 reports last week (up 357% from 6.1 weekly average), the highest z-score spike affecting city-managed infrastructure, suggesting park, library, or public facility deterioration requiring immediate assessment.
evidence: 28 maintenance or facility complaints last week vs. 6.1 weekly average (z-score: 4.34, severity: high)
Community board's repeated budget requests for 'Reconstruct or upgrade a building in a park' and library enhancements suggest chronic deferred maintenance
Generic category requires FOIL follow-up to determine whether complaints target Parks, NYPL, DCAS, or other agencies
reporting_angles: FOIL the 28 complaints to identify agency responsible and specific facilities affected — is this Prospect Heights Park, Brooklyn Public Library, or public restrooms?
Investigate whether single high-profile facility failure (e.g., locked restroom, broken equipment) triggered avalanche of related complaints.
